record.original_question: Determine whether there are only finitely many hyperkahler manifolds, up to deformation, in each dimension.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. There are finitely many hyperkahler manifolds (up to deformation) in each dimension.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A compact complex manifold X is called an irreducible holomorphic symplectic (hyperkähler) manifold if it is simply connected and H^0(X, Ω^2_X) is generated by a nowhere-degenerate holomorphic 2-form. Two such manifolds are said to be deformation equivalent if they can be connected by a smooth proper family of irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds over a connected base.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer n, there exist only finitely many deformation equivalence classes of irreducible holomorphic symplectic (hyperkähler) manifolds of complex dimension 2n.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that in each (even) complex dimension there are only finitely many deformation types of irreducible compact hyperkähler manifolds remains open in general. Partial results exist (e.g., Huybrechts' theorem giving finiteness once the Beauville–Bogomolov lattice is fixed; finiteness results for Lagrangian fibrations by Sawon and others; boundedness results via degeneration techniques). Currently only a small list of known examples is available in each dimension (Hilbert schemes of K3 points, generalized Kummer varieties, and O'Grady's two exceptional examples in dimensions 6 and 10).

status_evidence.title: Topological bounds on hyperkähler manifolds (Sawon, 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing the conjecture and partial finiteness/boundedness results for compact hyperkähler manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The finiteness-up-to-deformation conjecture is treated as an open problem with partial results.

status_evidence.title: Remarks on degenerations of hyper-Kähler manifolds (Kollár–Laza–Saccà–Voisin)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies degenerations of hyper-Kähler manifolds, providing partial results toward boundedness.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to address boundedness and finiteness questions for hyperkähler manifolds.

status_evidence.title: NSF CAREER: Finiteness for Hyperkahler Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Research project explicitly aimed at the finiteness conjecture for hyperkähler manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is recognized as an active open research problem.
